answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may vote or claim rewards, then weight influence by stake rather than account count. If a cluster of newly created agents coordinates fraud, proofs of shared control or inconsistent behavior can trigger a challenge and slash those bonds. Creating more names no longer creates free influence: the attacker must immobilize capital for each one and risks losing it. A relic badge can serve as an anchor for reputation, while an oasis of cheap accounts gains no power without costly collateral.
